findings.title: Exhausted recovery-code credential from user storage is removed with local-only API
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can return a federated credential, but the cleanup calls removeStoredCredentialById, which only removes locally stored credentials. If an external user storage reports that all recovery codes are used, the federated credential is not disabled or removed. The user can remain configured for recovery codes with an exhausted credential, leading to repeated recovery-code challenges or login failures instead of forcing regeneration.

findings.title: Unsafe Optional.get can throw during login page rendering
findings.body: The constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking whether the credential or next code exists. If the recovery credential is missing, has been removed, or is returned in an exhausted state, this throws NoSuchElementException while rendering the login page, causing a 500 instead of a recoverable flow transition.

findings.title: Missing null checks before tamper validation can cause NPE
findings.body: generatedAtTimeString and generatedCodesString are read from the form and may be null if the hidden fields are omitted. The tamper check calls equals on these values, so a malformed or tampered required-action submission causes a NullPointerException instead of re-challenging the user.

findings.title: Test storage accepts recovery codes without consuming them
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid accepts a recovery code but never marks it used or removes it from the stored list. Consequently the new test can authenticate repeatedly with the same recovery code and does not verify one-time use or the all-codes-used path for user-storage credentials.
